extracted.intended_audience: general readers and the public, plus potential contributors, advertisers, press contacts, and job applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational policies and procedural guidelines from The Onion's 'About' page covering submissions, contacts, careers, advertising, licensing, archives, and content/age/legal notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission policy — no outside submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: No, The Onion does not accept outside submissions of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Onion will not respond to any unsolicited submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information and unsolicited email policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Click here for information on contacting The Onion. Please note that unsolicited bulk email, email attachments, and junk email of any kind are not accepted, and will be filtered and immediately discarded upon receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the published contact channels rather than sending unsolicited attachments or bulk email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careers and résumé submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Onion Inc. regularly posts new openings on the Careers section of our website. On the exceedingly rare occasions that there are openings for editorial positions, those opportunities will be posted on our Careers page as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do not send résumés unless specifically told to do so in a job listing. Any unsolicited résumés will be immediately discarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback on content
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send all concerns to publicfeedback@theonion.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Onion cannot guarantee a response to any feedback to its content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising inquiries procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send all advertising inquiries to advertising@theonion.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please specify the business you would like to advertise, and the appropriate advertising sales representative will get back to you promptly. For more information regarding advertising opportunities consult the Media Kit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press/media inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Please send all inquiries to press@theonion.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media organizations should use the press contact for requests to cover The Onion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking engagements availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The writers and editors of America’s Finest News Source and its sister sites are available for speaking engagements at universities, conferences, and festivals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn more via the provided link; use the stated channel for booking or information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archives access and article requests
rubrics_metrics.description: This website contains all of The Onion’s articles published from early 1996 through the present. Browse by issue number, topic, section, or search the archive by keyword.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please send requests for articles and graphics from past issues, including those published before 1996, to archive@theonion.com. The Onion will attempt to answer but cannot guarantee a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and reprint restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion may not be reprinted or retransmitted in whole or in part without the express written consent of the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To license material from The Onion, send a request to permissions@theonion.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of names in stories
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion uses invented names in all of its stories, except in cases where public figures are being satirized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other use of real names is accidental and coincidental.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience age guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion is not intended for readers under 18 years of age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content is targeted to adults; younger readers are not the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal stance on satire
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not sue The Onion. The First Amendment protects satire as a form of free speech and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Onion emphasizes its satirical nature as a defense against legal action related to content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site availability and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Onion is an online-only publication and is no longer available in print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connect to The Onion via the website and listed social channels; books are separately available for purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sister sites and their scopes (informational)
rubrics_metrics.description: The A.V. Club is a sister site featuring pop culture commentary; ClickHole is a sister site featuring clickable, shareable content built to go viral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn more about each sister site via the provided links; this describes scope rather than submission rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and distribution channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Outside of TheOnion.com, you can connect via social media platforms such as Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, Youtube, Google+, Tumblr, Pinterest, and Vine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These channels are the official ways to follow and share The Onion's content online.
